_why: Commit 0f7ad05 claimed "Guard mutation-tested" for the ledger classifier and shipped NO spec in either store, which a fresh-context review found on 2026-09-10. The guard does bite -- deleting the branch fails its named test -- but a guard verified only by a session that has ended is invisible to the anchor sweep, and the sweep is what catches the ordinary edit that silently invalidates a spec. This makes the verification durable. Both mutations leave a file that still classifies and still prints a verdict-shaped line. The second is the more valuable: it restores the wrong alternative the source comment says was TRIED and rejected, so the spec pins the reasoning and not just the branch.

mutations.name: the-ledger-marker-is-not-read
mutations._mechanism: Drop the declaration check and a committed provenance ledger is swept as a spec. It has no `command`, so `_load_spec` raises and the WHOLE sweep goes ANCHORS_UNREADABLE -- which the pre-push hook blocks on, for every commit in the repository. The failure is not local to the ledger: one file takes out the gate for everyone.

mutations.name: the-ledger-is-INFERRED-instead-of-declared
mutations._mechanism: The wrong alternative, restored -- the source comment says this was tried and is provably wrong, and without a mutation nothing stops a future editor trying it again. Keying on the ABSENCE of `file`/`find` looks like it identifies a ledger, but a HALF-WRITTEN SPEC has the same shape: AC-6.3's `{"mutations": [{"name": "has no command"}]}` is reclassified as not-a-spec and vanishes from the sweep silently. That is the exact hole the fail-closed default exists to keep shut, so this mutation must be killed by the AC-6.3 test rather than by the ledger's own.
mutations.replace: if all(not m.get("file") and not m.get("find") for m in (data.get("mutations") or [{}])):
